A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DualGraph research work. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original DualGraph evaluations on three research benchmarks, iterative-outline ablations, and token-cost measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original evaluations and adds benchmark results, component ablations, citation and graph-extraction analyses, and a human evaluation of judge reliability.

M1.justification: The dual-graph workflow, search-chain scoring equations, report generation, and prompt templates remain unchanged. Added explanations of chain filtering, quota backfilling, and self-correction do not establish a changed implementation; the LightRAG substitution is an experimental variant.

E1.justification: v2 adds DeepResearch Bench II alongside the three retained benchmark datasets. This extends evaluation within text-based, long-form research; additional application domains, languages, or modalities are not documented.

E2.justification: WebWeaver and WebShaper become evaluated comparators in Tables 1–2. v2 also tests a LightRAG-based KG-construction variant and expands cost comparisons to other research systems. These additions substantially strengthen comparison with relevant alternative approaches; Graph-R1, GraphSearch, and GraphAgent remain discussion-only references.

E3.justification: New protocols include Bench II's rubric metrics, GPT-5 evaluations on DeepResearchGym/DeepConsult, fixed-five-round ablations with shared initialization, joint-citation scoring on 20 cases, and five-annotator review of 10 evaluation cases. These extend the evaluation design; the original benchmark judging models are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's KG/no-KG analyses, v2 tests enrichment, exploration, topology-based selection, and LightRAG construction separately (Figure 3). Appendices A.2, F, and G add citation-protocol analysis, an audit of 6,014 extracted triplets with a correction example, and human validation of LLM judging.

E5.justification: Appendix G introduces inter-annotator reliability estimation, reporting Gwet's AC1 of 0.95 alongside unanimous and individual agreement rates. Neither version reports repeated-run performance uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing headline scores, including 53.08 RACE, remain. v2 adds 41.48 Total on Bench II, GPT-5 scores of 96.52 on DeepResearchGym and 6.84 on DeepConsult, and new ablation/reliability results. Mean stopping iterations change from 3.20/3.81 to 3.23/3.88. Cost results are replaced with measurements on a specified 20-case subset, not an established same-setting cost increase.

T1.justification: New Appendix D defines candidate search spaces, derives cardinality/budget bounds, and argues for monotonic gap resolution and practical convergence. This is a limited formal extension beyond v1's retained scoring equations, without a proved convergence guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction expand the empirical claim from three to four benchmarks and introduce the Bench II result. Separating knowledge from outline structure and using graph-driven exploration remain the central contributions; the conclusion is substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v1 interprets lower citation accuracy as a precision–coverage tradeoff; v2 attributes it mainly to independent-citation scoring, supported by joint evaluation. New discussions explain component contributions, criticize retrieval-oriented KG construction for gap detection, and qualify extraction-error risks through claimed self-correction. The cost–quality tradeoff also receives fuller treatment.

D1.justification: v2 adds module-level runtimes and quota-backfilling details. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit 10-query budgets for each graph, top-5 URL setting, and separate no-KG pseudocode. Backend identifiers, retrieval pipeline, and prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Bench II, LightRAG, Graph-R1, GraphSearch, and GraphAgent. Appendix A.4 sharpens the distinction between evolving graph-guided research planning and graph retrieval over fixed corpora. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or consolidate duplicate entries.

P1.justification: The main section order and most existing prose remain. v2 makes localized wording, affiliation, and cross-reference corrections, expands appendix organization, and relocates the cost analysis, case trajectory, and unchanged prompt templates.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel ablation Figure 3, Bench II Table 3, and extraction-error Table 7. It replaces the compact cost table with Tables 5–6, expands benchmark tables, and adds an Iter 1 column to the stopping table. Original Figures 3–4 are retained as Figures 4–5.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's broad KG/no-KG comparison: relevant direct baselines, component ablations, citation and extraction audits, and human checking address important weaknesses in attributing and trusting the reported gains. Expanded cost measurements clarify practical tradeoffs. These benefits outweigh the loss of explicit retrieval-budget settings, although the small human audit and heuristic convergence argument leave limitations.
